title: High Resolution Depth Profile Scanning of Plankton Organisms
author: Kvæstad, Hagemann, et al.

steps.title: Transport and assemble platform
steps.instruction: Move the VERTILICE modules to the field site and assemble the system at the land facility (coordinates 63.141914, 8.220516).

substeps.instruction: Load modules onto a crane boat.
Transport to the salmon sea‑cage location.
Unpack and assemble the 11‑meter acrylic tube and supporting hardware.

steps.title: Secure rig in net‑pen
steps.instruction: Anchor the assembled rig inside the net‑pen using six ropes.

substeps.instruction: Tie four ropes to hold the rig in the middle of the pen.
Tie two additional ropes to keep the frame horizontal.

steps.title: Test overcurrent protection
steps.instruction: Adjust and verify the overcurrent protection unit before starting the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Manually hold back the sled until the protection unit trips.
Confirm that the motor stops when the unit triggers.

steps.title: Load copepodites into tube
steps.instruction: Introduce 876 sea‑lice copepodites (size 0.5–10 mm) into the acrylic tube.

steps.title: Configure scanning schedule
steps.instruction: Program the system to acquire two scans per hour (every 30 min) from 03 May to 07 May 2022.

substeps.instruction: Set total expected scans to 179.
Enable simultaneous recording of light intensity, temperature, and copepodite images.

steps.title: Mid‑experiment maintenance break
steps.instruction: On 04 May, pause the experiment for two hours to repair a leak in the underwater housing.

steps.title: Retrieve raw data
steps.instruction: After the trial, copy all scan files from the external hard drive to a processing computer.

steps.title: Bin measurements into depth intervals
steps.instruction: For each scan, aggregate copepodite counts, light, and temperature into 10 cm vertical depth bins and divide by the number of measurements in each bin.

steps.title: Calculate and subtract average profile
steps.instruction: Create an average copepodite density profile and remove it from each individual scan.

substeps.instruction: Sum each scan’s 10‑cm bins across all complete scans (matching nth bin with nth bin).
Divide the summed values by the number of complete scans (165) to obtain the average profile.
Subtract this average profile from every scan.
Set any resulting negative bin values to zero.

steps.title: Quality‑control scan set
steps.instruction: Identify and discard scans that are unusable.

substeps.instruction: Remove 4 scans containing unwanted particles in the tube.
Remove 10 scans with incomplete data due to delayed camera initialization or faulty limit switch.
Retain the remaining 165 complete scans for analysis.

steps.title: Record environmental parameters
steps.instruction: Log temperature and light data and note biological limits relevant to the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Temperature range for infective copepodite stage: 7–10 °C (duration 13–14 days).
Copepodite age at start of experiment: up to 6 days.

steps.title: Document system limitations
steps.instruction: Note hardware‑related factors that may affect detection counts.

substeps.instruction: The acrylic tube is 11 m long and assembled from 2‑m sections spliced with a 5 cm sleeve; splices occur at ~1, 3, 5, 7, 9 m depth, creating blind spots covering ~2 % of total area.
Lens focal length is slightly smaller than the tube diameter, leaving a narrow region along the inner and outer walls out of focus.
Detected copepodite counts per scan vary between 500–800; orientation parallel to the camera can cause under‑counting.
